items.title: Democrat Scott Colom flips Mississippi Senate seat
items.feedTitle: Democrats rally around Colom's historic Mississippi victory
items.summary: Democrat Scott Colom defeated Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi's closely watched Senate race, becoming the state's first Black senator since Reconstruction. The victory, confirmed after a prolonged ballot count, represents a historic flip in a reliably Republican state and marks Democrats' eighth Senate seat gain in the midterms. The narrow margin victory surprised political analysts and energized Democratic voters nationwide.

items.title: Brooklyn building collapse kills two, traps occupants
items.feedTitle: Dangerous search for survivors continues after deadly building collapse in Brooklyn
items.summary: A three-story building collapsed in Brooklyn on Wednesday near a construction site, killing at least two people and injuring several others. Firefighters dug through rubble searching for additional survivors, with reports indicating people were trapped in the wreckage. The cause of the collapse remains under investigation as rescue operations continued.

items.title: Historic SS United States sinks off Florida coast
items.feedTitle: World's fastest ocean liner is sunk to break another record: largest artificial reef
items.summary: The SS United States, the world's fastest ocean liner which set a trans-Atlantic speed record in 1952, was intentionally sunk off the Florida coast on Wednesday. The ship will now serve as the world's largest artificial ocean reef and diving destination. The sinking concluded decades-long efforts to preserve the historic vessel as efforts to turn it into a museum ultimately failed.

items.title: Trump defends Iran war at Arlington cemetery event
items.feedTitle: Trump defends his war policies in speech at Arlington National Cemetery
items.summary: Trump defended his administration's war policies during a Veterans Day speech at Arlington National Cemetery, stating the Iran conflict will end "when we want to end it." The address drew attention when his entourage was reprimanded by an Army sentinel for failing to maintain appropriate decorum at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. Trump also promoted his proposed 250-foot arch, suggesting it could be dedicated to military veterans.

stlouis.title: St. Luke's Hospital to merge with BJC Health
stlouis.feedTitle: St. Luke’s Hospital to merge with St. Louis healthcare giant BJC
stlouis.summary: St. Luke's Hospital announced a letter of intent to merge with BJC Health, St. Louis's largest healthcare system, in a move aimed at strengthening healthcare delivery across the region. The merger, subject to regulatory approval, will combine two major hospital networks serving the metro area. The deal signals ongoing consolidation in the region's healthcare landscape as systems seek to improve efficiency and service.

stlouis.title: St. Louis doctors urge vaccination as measles rises
stlouis.feedTitle: St. Louis doctors urge vaccination as US measles cases rise
stlouis.summary: Physicians in the St. Louis region are urging residents to get vaccinated as measles cases rise across the United States. The public health push comes amid concerns about declining vaccination rates and the highly contagious nature of the disease. Local health officials are emphasizing prevention measures to protect vulnerable populations.

stlouis.title: Nine St. Louis public schools set to close
stlouis.feedTitle: Nine St. Louis public schools to close
stlouis.summary: Nine schools within the St. Louis Public School District are scheduled to close, according to reporting from the St. Louis American. The closures reflect ongoing challenges in the district related to enrollment or financial pressures. Details on the specific schools and timeline for closure were not fully elaborated in available reporting.

items.title: Democrat Scott Colom unseats Mississippi Republican senator
items.feedTitle: Democrat Scott Colom unseats Cindy Hyde-Smith in stunning Mississippi Senate win
items.summary: Democrat Scott Colom defeated incumbent Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi after a closely contested race decided by razor-thin margin, becoming the state's first Black senator since Reconstruction. The historic victory flipped another U.S. Senate seat for Democrats following the midterm elections, in a state that has not elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1982. The result surprised political observers given Mississippi's longtime Republican lean.

items.title: Brooklyn building collapses, killing at least two people
items.feedTitle: Brooklyn building collapse kills at least two people and traps others in wreckage
items.summary: A three-story building in Brooklyn collapsed near a construction site on Wednesday, killing at least two people and trapping others in the rubble. Firefighters worked to dig through debris as rescue efforts continued, with several people reported in critical condition. The cause of the collapse remains under investigation.

items.title: Iran threatens strikes on U.S. bases in Europe
items.feedTitle: Iran issues 'ominous' new threat to strike European countries home to US military bases
items.summary: Iran's security chief warned that Tehran would strike U.S. military bases in Europe if they are used to attack Iran, escalating rhetoric amid the ongoing Iran-U.S. tensions. The threat comes as officials indicate Iran may take pre-emptive action if diplomatic stalemate continues. The warning suggests Iran views European-based U.S. military infrastructure as fair targets in any resumed conflict.

items.title: Spain's first general strike in 14 years erupts
items.feedTitle: Clashes erupt in Barcelona after thousands join Spain general strike
items.summary: Millions of Spaniards participated in the country's first general strike in 14 years on Wednesday, protesting soaring housing costs and the high cost of living. The 24-hour stoppage drew significant participation as labor unions mobilized workers weeks before an election in which the far right could gain power. Clashes erupted in Barcelona as protesters hurled fireworks and set rubbish bins ablaze.

items.title: Russia and Ukraine agree to largest prisoner exchange
items.feedTitle: Russia and Ukraine agree to a large prisoner exchange as talks end with no major breakthrough
items.summary: Russia and Ukraine agreed to exchange the largest group of prisoners of war to date as two days of U.S.-brokered talks concluded in Abu Dhabi, though the discussions produced no major breakthrough toward ending the five-year-old full-scale invasion. U.S. envoys are scheduled to separately meet with Putin in Moscow and Zelenskyy in Dublin on Thursday. The prisoner deal represents progress on a discrete issue even as broader peace negotiations remain stalled.

items.title: India simplifies visa norms, cuts application forms
items.feedTitle: India simplifies visa norms; categories cut, forms to be 70% leaner
items.summary: India announced simplified visa procedures, reducing visa categories from 13 to 9 and cutting application form fields by 65-70%, the Ministry of Home Affairs said. The reform aims to draw more foreign visitors and streamline the application process. The move is intended to make India a more attractive destination for tourism and business while maintaining security screening.

items.title: India's direct tax collection rises 12% through November
items.feedTitle: Net direct tax collection grows 12% to Rs 14.42 lakh crore till November 10, touches 53% of FY27 target
items.summary: Net direct tax collection grew 12% to reach ₹14.42 lakh crore as of November 10, touching 53% of the fiscal year 2027 target, according to government data. The strong growth in tax receipts reflects ongoing economic activity and improved compliance. The figure suggests the government remains on track to meet its full-year collection goals.

items.title: Canada trade minister to visit India for pact talks
items.feedTitle: Confident of trade pact ahead of PM Modi's trip: Canada envoy
items.summary: Canada's trade minister is set to visit India to advance negotiations for a proposed bilateral trade agreement, according to reporting from the Canadian High Commission in New Delhi. The visit comes ahead of a planned trip by Indian PM Modi to Canada. Officials expressed confidence that a trade pact is achievable in the near term.

items.title: Cabinet clears ₹3,230-crore museum with largest display
items.feedTitle: Cabinet clears Rs 3,230-crore museum with world’s largest display area
items.summary: India's Cabinet approved a ₹3,230-crore project to develop the Yug Yugeen Bharat Museum at the North and South Block complex, featuring the world's largest display area for a museum. The facility will showcase Indian heritage and civilization. The approval marks a major cultural investment by the government.

items.title: Indian Navy conducts Sea Vigil-26 coastal security test
items.feedTitle: Navy kicks off ‘Sea Vigil-26’ to test India’s coastal security preparedness post-26/11
items.summary: The Indian Navy initiated 'Sea Vigil-26' exercise to test the country's coastal security preparedness following the 2008 Mumbai terror attacks (26/11). The annual drill assesses India's ability to detect and respond to maritime threats. The exercise involves coordination between naval and coast guard units across Indian waters.

immigration.title: IBM ends H-1B, green card sponsorship for consulting
immigration.feedTitle: IBM to end visa and green-card sponsorship for most U.S. Consulting roles
immigration.summary: IBM announced it will discontinue H-1B visa and green card sponsorship for most roles in its consulting division, citing the availability of U.S. talent. The move affects both prospective hires and existing visa holders seeking green card sponsorship. The decision reflects broader industry pressure to reduce reliance on visa-sponsored workers, though IBM's core technology divisions continue sponsoring visas (status: finalized, in effect).

immigration.title: DHS proposes scrapping H-1B 60-day grace period
immigration.feedTitle: Is the H-1B 60-day grace period ending? Not yet, but DHS has proposed scrapping it
immigration.summary: The Department of Homeland Security has proposed eliminating the 60-day grace period that allows H-1B visa holders to remain in the U.S. after job termination while seeking new employment or filing appeals. The proposal has drawn over 31,000 public comments, with critics warning the change would force workers to leave immediately upon job loss (status: proposed, not final—pending federal review and public comment period closure).

immigration.title: Wage hike rule for H-1B, green card applicants advances
immigration.feedTitle: H-1B, green card applicants may face potential wage hikes as rule advances for federal review | Hindustan Times
immigration.summary: A proposed Department of Labor rule requiring wage hikes for H-1B and employment-based green card applicants has advanced for federal review. The rule aims to ensure workers are paid market rates, though critics question whether it will force employers to hire more American workers or simply reduce visa sponsorships (status: proposed, advancing through federal review process).

items.title: Nvidia stock plunges as board debates CEO's future
items.feedTitle: Jensen Huang Said to Have Had Relationship With Nvidia Executive Who Reports to Him
items.summary: Nvidia shares fell 8% in after-hours trading after reports that the company's board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang following revelations of affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. Huang's potential departure would create a leadership vacuum at the $4 trillion chipmaker he co-founded 33 years ago. The board is reportedly meeting to decide his future amid concerns over national security implications and governance failings.

items.title: Poundland owner extracted millions amid crisis
items.feedTitle: Poundland set for more time to secure a rescue deal as emergency talks continue
items.summary: The owner of UK budget retailer Poundland extracted millions of pounds from the chain while it teetered on a "knife-edge," according to MPs investigating the company's financial distress. Poundland management is seeking a two-week extension of legal protection from creditors in high court as it attempts to secure a rescue deal. The retailer faces potential collapse absent a successful restructuring.

U.S. equities rallied midweek with the Nasdaq surging over 1% on strong AI infrastructure demand (CoreWeave results), though Nvidia shares dropped 8% after-hours over CEO succession concerns. India's Sensex jumped 773 points to a nine-month high on record foreign portfolio investor inflows and cheaper oil. Watch: Nvidia board's formal decision on Jensen Huang's fate (could come within 24 hours), U.S. inflation data due Friday, and Anthropic IPO pricing (1 week away).

cards.title: The Cost of Delayed Accountability
cards.insight: Jensen Huang's board delay in addressing the affair allegations—first admitted publicly, then a second one emerges—demonstrates how postponing hard decisions compounds reputational damage. Each news cycle extends the leadership crisis rather than resolving it. Indecision signals weakness to investors, employees, and rivals.
cards.takeaway: When facing serious misconduct or competency issues in leadership, swift transparent action—even if painful—restores confidence faster than lingering uncertainty.

cards.title: Momentum vs. Deliberation
cards.insight: The Sensex's nine-month high and Nasdaq's AI rebound show how quickly sentiment reverses when external pressures ease (oil prices, Iran peace hopes). Yet these reversals often outlrun fundamentals. Markets can swing on hope before clarity emerges on whether peace talks or tech board decisions will actually succeed.
cards.takeaway: Distinguish between tactical rallies driven by sentiment shifts and strategic moves grounded in operational or political reality—they require different portfolio responses.

cards.title: Regulatory Capture Through Attrition
cards.insight: IBM's unilateral decision to end H-1B sponsorship, ahead of any formal rule change, shows how companies can outrun regulators by voluntarily tightening practices. This preempts stricter mandates and avoids enforcement risk—but also shapes labor markets before policy formally changes. Anticipation becomes self-fulfilling.
cards.takeaway: Watch industry behavior as a leading signal of where regulation is heading; voluntary compliance often precedes formal rules and sets the tone for competitors.

cards.title: The Succession Vacuum
cards.insight: Nvidia's lack of succession plan for Huang after 33 years illustrates a common governance failure: founder-led tech companies often assume perpetual leadership, leaving the board without a bench of ready replacements. When crisis forces a change, the void is deep and the transition chaotic.
cards.takeaway: For any organization dependent on a single leader, maintain a documented succession pipeline independent of whether that leader ever leaves—it's a core risk mitigation tool.

ai.title: Nvidia board prepares to remove CEO Jensen Huang
ai.feedTitle: Nvidia’s stock drops as board reportedly preps to oust CEO Jensen Huang
ai.summary: Nvidia's board is reportedly preparing to oust founder and CEO Jensen Huang after 33 years, following revelations of affairs including one with a woman accused of being a Chinese intelligence agent. The decision could come as early as Wednesday. Huang's removal would leave a significant leadership vacuum at the $4 trillion chipmaker and raise succession planning concerns among investors and analysts.

ai.title: Anthropic launches models, workplace tools before IPO
ai.feedTitle: With IPO looming, Anthropic launches new AI models, workplace tools
ai.summary: Anthropic, preparing for its imminent IPO, launched new AI models and workplace tools designed to compete with established players. The company is ramping up product offerings as it seeks to demonstrate revenue growth and market potential to public investors. The timing underscores Anthropic's push to prove its technology and business model merit a high valuation.

ai.title: CoreWeave turns to customer prepayments for funding
ai.feedTitle: CoreWeave turns to customer prepayments, shorter contracts to fund AI growth
ai.summary: GPU rental company CoreWeave is increasingly asking customers to pay up front and is borrowing against specific contracts to fund AI infrastructure growth, according to third-quarter earnings. The company is also exploring shorter-term deals that could lead to higher prices. The strategy reflects CoreWeave's need to manage cash flow amid rapid scaling of AI compute capacity.

ai.title: Fractile raises $720 million for AI chip development
ai.feedTitle: With $720M round, Britain’s Fractile gets a leg up in the race for AI chips
ai.summary: British AI chip startup Fractile secured $720 million in funding, becoming one of the top-funded players in the race to develop purpose-built chips for artificial intelligence. The capital will accelerate Fractile's efforts to challenge Nvidia's dominance in AI semiconductor design. The funding reflects investor appetite for alternatives to Nvidia's market-leading GPU architecture.

ai.title: Blacklisted Chinese university bought Nvidia AI chips
ai.feedTitle: A blacklisted Chinese university with military ties bought Nvidia AI chips despite U.S. ban
ai.summary: A blacklisted Chinese university with military ties purchased two Nvidia H200 AI chips worth $123,000 despite being subject to U.S. export controls, according to reporting. The acquisition highlights potential breaches in enforcement of technology restrictions aimed at limiting China's AI development. U.S. authorities are investigating how the chips reached the restricted institution.
